chunks: Samaah narrated from Abu Basir from Abu Jafar (peace be upon him)

Regarding His saying, the Almighty and Majestic: 'But if any remission is made by the brother of the slain, then grant [him] a suitable follow-up.' I asked: 'What is that thing?' He said: 'It is when a man accepts the blood money. Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, commanded the one who has the right to pursue it in a good manner and not to make it difficult, and He commanded the one who owes the right not to wrong him and to pay it to him with kindness when he becomes able.'
But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
He said: 'It is the man who accepts the blood money or agrees to a settlement, and then later comes back to mutilate or kill. Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, has promised him a painful punishment.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'But if any remission is made...' mean in the context of blood money and retaliation?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'remission' is interpreted as the heir's acceptance of blood money, establishing a mutual covenant of fairness where the payer avoids hardship and the recipient avoids oppression. The subsequent 'transgression' is specifically defined as the heir violating this agreement by killing or mutilating the payer after receiving the payment, highlighting the legal weight of post-settlement conduct. This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence) and *adl* (justice) in financial settlements, moving beyond mere legal compliance to ethical integrity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5218 - Samaah narrated from Abu Basir from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic:
"But if any remission is made by the brother of the slain, then grant [him] a suitable follow-up" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:178).
I asked: "What is that 'remission'?"
Imam (as) said: "It is when a person accepts the blood money (diyyah). Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, commanded the one who has the right (the victim's heir) to pursue it in a good manner and not to make it difficult, and He (swt) commanded the one who owes the blood money not to wrong him and to pay it with kindness when he becomes able to do so."
I then asked: "What about Allah's (swt) saying:
'But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment'?"
(Surah Al-Baqarah 2:178).
Imam (as) said: "This refers to the person who accepts the blood money or agrees to a settlement and then later comes back to mutilate or kill (the killer). Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has promised him a painful punishment."
